content: # Plain Plain is a customer support platform for B2B and technical SaaS companies, built entirely on its own public GraphQL API so there is full parity between what the product UI and the API can do. It unifies support across email, chat, Slack, and API-created threads, with customers, companies, tenants, tiers and SLAs, labels, help center articles, snippets, tasks, and events as first-class entities. Developers integrate via a Relay-style GraphQL API (bearer API keys with fine-grained permissions), typed TypeScript and Go SDKs, a CLI, customer-card UI components, HMAC-signed webhooks, a hosted MCP server, and an official agent skill. This profile was enriched from Plain's public developer surface. Plain is listed with 1 API on the [APIs.io](https://apis.io/) network. Tagged areas include Company, Customer Service, Help Desk, Support, and Software-as-a-Service. The Plain catalog on APIs.io includes 1 event-driven AsyncAPI specification. Plain’s developer surface includes documentation, API reference, getting-started guide, engineering blog, support, pricing, changelog, and 32 more developer resources. **Pull Plain's APIs, OpenAPI, scores and pricing into your own code or AI agent** with a free APIs.io key — sign in with [GitHub](https://apis.io/api/v1/auth/login?provider=github), [Google](https://apis.io/api/v1/auth/login?provider=google) or [LinkedIn](https://apis.io/api/v1/auth/login?provider=linkedin). No form to fill in; signing in shares your email address with us ([Privacy](https://apis.io/privacy/)). Paid **1** API **1** MCP Servers **1** Agent Skills **Regulatory Posture applies to this provider.** Its tags matched the **Horizontal (data, software, accessibility, platform)** regime, so Regulatory Posture carries 15 points of the composite. If this regime is wrong for your business, say so on your [provider repo](https://github.com/api-evangelist/plain) — the [applicability map](https://apis.io/rating/#regulatory) is public and we will correct it. **Create-or-Update Ergonomics could not be measured.** We hold no machine-readable contract for this provider to read, so there is nothing to measure a write surface against. Excluded rather than scored zero: never-measured and measured-empty are different facts. Publishing an OpenAPI is what makes this facet — and several others — scorable at all. **The six quality facets above are damped to 85 points between them**, because the conditional facet above carries the other 15. That is why each facet's contribution is shown against a damped maximum: raising a quality facet moves the composite by 85% of its nominal weight, not 100%. The full arithmetic is at [apis.io/rating/](https://apis.io/rating/#regulatory-math). **Show this score on your site.** [![Kin Score badge preview for Plain](https://apis.io/badge/plain/card.svg)](https://apis.io/badge/plain/) It updates itself when the score changes. Paste this where you link to your API docs: ``` ``` Other styles, a README pill and a shields.io endpoint are on [the badge page](https://apis.io/badge/plain/). **Raise your score.** Agent readiness — checks not met, largest first (exact, from this profile): - [Agentic Access Contract](https://apis.io/rating/dimensions/agentic-access/) +10 pts — agentic_access artifact present (x-agentic-access), graded by author Ask about this → - [Idempotency](https://apis.io/rating/dimensions/idempotency/) +9 pts — OpenAPI mutating operations declare an idempotency key — a header, a request-body property, or a named de-duplication token whose own description says so (verified); else common[].type matches /idempoten/i (documented) Ask about this → - [A2A Agent Card](https://apis.io/rating/dimensions/agent-card/) +8 pts — a2a/-a2a.yml manifest, graded on conformance.grade against A2A 1.0.0 Ask about this → - [Request/Response Examples](https://apis.io/rating/dimensions/openapi-examples/) +7 pts — share of operations carrying request/response examples; else an Examples / Code Samples link Ask about this → - [Rate-Limit Signaling](https://apis.io/rating/dimensions/rate-limit-signal/) +7 pts — OpenAPI responses document X-RateLimit-* / RateLimit headers (verified), else a rate_limits artifact or RateLimits link (documented) Ask about this → - [Documented Reversibility](https://apis.io/rating/dimensions/reversibility-documented/) +6 pts — a reversal operation in the contract, graded up when a window is documented too Ask about this → 5 more unmet checks in the Agent Readiness table above. Kin Score — facets with the most composite points still available (weight × headroom): - [Contract Quality](https://apis.io/rating/facets/contract-quality/) scores 51.0 — up to +12.3 composite points Ask about this → - [Contract Governance](https://apis.io/rating/facets/contract-governance/) scores 4.5 — up to +11.5 composite points Ask about this → - [Operational Transparency](https://apis.io/rating/facets/operational-transparency/) scores 40.5 — up to +7.7 composite points Ask about this → **Not sure how this applies to your stack?** Ask about any one item. Kin Lane reads every question, looks at your profile and your situation, and replies with what a fix would take — scoped to that one area, priced up front, yours whether you ship it or not. Undeclared means we found nothing we can read, so there is no number: we never infer integrations. ## Used by apps 3 of the reference apps in [Applications](https://apis.io/applications/), across 3 categories, integrate with this provider, read from each app's own code, build or integrations page. - [Documenso](https://apis.io/applications/e-signature-contracts/documenso/) E-signature & Contract Management - [Dub](https://apis.io/applications/url-shortener-links/dub/) Link Management & URL Shorteners - [Polar](https://apis.io/applications/subscription-billing/polar/) Subscription Billing & Payments Ops ## Standards implemented 6 Standards this provider implements or carries. De facto ones are profiled and measured by the [API Commons](https://apicommons.org/standards/); formal ones come from the [standards directory](https://apis.io/standards/#formal) and are linked by the provider's own tags. The evidence column says how each claim was established — not that it was made. ## APIs 1 Individual APIs this provider publishes, each with its own machine-readable definition. ## MCP Servers 1 Model Context Protocol servers that expose these APIs to AI agents. ## Agent Skills 1 Packaged agent skills for driving this provider's APIs from an AI assistant. ## Plain API pricing Prices published by Plain, read 2026-10-28 from [www.plain.com/pricing](https://www.plain.com/pricing). | Plan | Price | |---|---| | Foundation | $45/user/month billed annually Includes: 1,000 credits / month; Member seats up to 5; Viewer seats unlimited | | Horizon | $99/user/month billed annually Includes: 2,500 credits / month; Member seats minimum 3, up to 10 | | Frontier | Custom Includes: Custom credits; Custom member seats | **Billed by:** user · [FinOps profile →](https://apis.io/finops/plain/plain-finops/) ## Pricing Plans 2 Published pricing tiers and plan structures. ## Terms of Service 1 What its API terms permit and prohibit, quoted from its own page. ## Privacy & Data 1 Its role, the data it processes, retention and transfers, quoted from its own privacy page. ## Compliance 1 Attestations the provider states (SOC 2, ISO 27001 and others), quoted from its own trust page. APIs.io verifies none of them. ## Eligibility 1 Who may sign up and where, quoted from its own terms. ## AI Preferences 1 Its stance on AI training, inference and agents, quoted from its own pages. ## Data License 1 How its data and outputs may be reused, quoted from its own terms. ## FinOps 1 Cost, billing, and metering signals for API financial operations. ## Event Specifications 1 AsyncAPI definitions for this provider's event-driven and streaming APIs. ## Security Posture 3 Authentication, domain security, vulnerability disclosure, and trust-center signals. ## Resources ### Source (apis.yml) ## Plain API — frequently asked questions ### Does Plain have an API? Yes. APIs.io lists 1 API from Plain, including Plain Core GraphQL API. ### How do I authenticate with the Plain API? Plain documents its authentication (apiKey/oauth2/mutualTLS · 4 schemes). The details are profiled on APIs.io as Plain Authentication. ### How much does the Plain API cost? Plain publishes its prices; its Foundation plan is $45/user/month billed annually as of 2026-10-28. APIs.io lists 3 pricing plans for Plain, with each plan's price, limits and inclusions under Pricing on this page. ### Does Plain have an MCP server? Yes. APIs.io lists 1 MCP server for Plain: Remote MCP server at mcp.plain.com over HTTP; 30 tools listed. ### Is the Plain API ready for AI agents? Plain has a Kin Score of 61.8 out of 100 (strong) and an Agent Readiness score of 50.3 (agent-ready), scored by API Evangelist on 2026-11-21. ## Work with this as data Every provider here is available over the APIs.io API and to AI agents over MCP. #### MCP server One button, every client — Claude, Cursor, VS Code and the rest. `https://apis.io/mcp` #### Tools for providers 9 MCP tools reach this - `find_providers`Browse and filter every provider in the catalog. - `get_provider_artifacts`Every artifact this provider publishes, grouped by type. - `get_provider_operations`Every operation across all of their OpenAPIs — one call instead of parsing every spec. - `get_provider_tools`Every MCP tool they ship, with the operation each wraps. - `get_provider_evidence`How each part of their score was established. Free — the basis for a claim should not sit behind it. - `get_provider_rating`PRO — composite, band, trend and facet scores. - `apis_io_search`START HERE — APIs, providers and tags for one query, each with its total. - `resolve`Turn a domain, URL or GitHub org into the provider it belongs to. - `find_cohorts`Every scored population of providers in the catalog. [All 92 tools →](https://apis.io/developer/mcp-server/) #### Call it yourself curl for this page This provider ``` curl "https://apis.io/api/v1/providers/plain" ``` All providers ``` curl "https://apis.io/api/v1/providers?limit=25" ``` Every operation they expose ``` curl "https://apis.io/api/v1/providers/plain/operations?limit=25" ``` How their score was established ``` curl "https://apis.io/api/v1/providers/plain/evidence" ``` Calls without `X-API-Key` need no key. Calls with it need a paid plan — [get a key](https://apis.io/developer/account/?access=1). #### Get an API key Free tier, no form to fill in. Signing in shares your email address with us — we store it to create your key and to recognise you if you sign in with another provider. **By signing up you are subscribing to the APIs.io and API Evangelist newsletters** — you can unsubscribe from any issue. See our [Privacy Policy](https://apis.io/privacy/) and [Terms](https://apis.io/terms/). A second provider on the same verified email joins the account you already have.
